newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil - Tight supply seen stoking prices.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil - Tight supply seen stoking prices.

text.p: Prospects of higher demand for the Christmas holiday period and tight supply in the Philippines are expected to stoke firmer coconut oil prices this week, traders said on Monday.
"As far as we are concerned, coconut oil supply from the Philippines to Rotterdam and the U.S. markets is over for December," said a trader for a large oil miller.
"And, there's still a lot of demand for December despite fresh deliveries in Rotterdam last month," he added.
Traders said they expected coconut oil prices to rise by an average of US$30 to $40 a tonne CIF this week.
"With European buyers unsure of the stability and availability of raw materials in the Philippines, I expect a bigger price gap between spot prices and forwards," one said.
Coconut oil for October/November shipment was last traded at $855 a tonne CIF Europe last week as against $760 a tonne for December/January shipment, the trader added.
Manila-based traders said the next delivery of coconut oil in Rotterdam is scheduled on December 21.
MV Stolt Sapphire, with a meagre cargo of 3,000 tonnes of coconut oil, left the country on November 6 and is scheduled to arrive in Rotterdam on December 21, traders said.
"Between now and the 21st of December, there's nothing for Rotterdam," a trader said.
The next big shipment of oil is due to arrive in Rotterdam on January 5, 1997 aboard MV Sun Sapphire, which has a cargo of 28,000 tonnes, traders said.
MV Kenwood Park, with a cargo of between 30,000 to 38,000 tonnes of coconut oil, is expected to arrive in Rotterdam this week. The ship was expected in Europe last week.
"But the ship's (MV Kenwood Park's) cargo has been sold out" before its arrival, said one trader.
Philippine traders said coconut oil stocks in Rotterdam are only 14,000 tonnes despite fresh deliveries of about 42,000 tonnes from both the MV Star Sapphire and MV Batumi.
Coconut oil stocks in the U.S. market have reached between 35,000 to 40,000 tonnes, they said. Demand in the U.S. and Europe reaches about 45,000 tonnes each per month.

Traders said they expected coconut oil production from the Philippines to pick up in the second half of 1997 after output slumped badly this year as a result of the typhoons which hit coconut farms on Luzon island in 1995.

Philippine coconut oil exports in the first 11 months of the year reached 741,208 tonnes compared with 1,222,740 tonnes in the same period last year, preliminary data released on Monday by the trade group United Coconut Associations of the Philippines Inc (UCAP) showed.
For November alone, the country's coconut oil exports were 85,025 tonnes compared with 95,171 tonnes for the same peiod of 1995.
Manila vegetable oil dealers said the figures were within their expectations.
"The November coconut oil export figure was slightly higher compared to previous months due to carry over stocks from October," one trader said.
Delays in shipping coconut oil in October were carried over in November, the trader added.
The trader said he expected coconut oil exports to reach 820,000 tonnes this year from 1.334 million tonnes in 1995.
